quotes.text: Make sure the location’s `fr_meal_vouchers_conecs_payments` capability status is `active` before saving payment details.
Pass this location ID in `setup_details[location]` when creating the SetupIntent in the same sandbox.

old_evidence.text: You can test different scenarios with the SIRET passed into `setup_details[benefit][fr_meal_voucher][siret]`.

findings: Both captures document Payment Element and SetupIntent saving without a purchase for Bimpli, Pluxee and Up Déjeuner in private preview. November explicitly adds the waitlist, preview Stripe API version 2026-05-27.preview or later, a per-restaurant/store PaymentLocation set up through the API and an active fr_meal_vouchers_conecs_payments capability. Preview access, location capability and payment-method eligibility are distinct requirements (new raw lines 5-37).

Server SetupIntent creation takes Customer ID, setup_details[location] and setup_details[benefit][fr_meal_voucher][enabled]=if_payment_method_is_eligible. The server sends only the SetupIntent client secret to the client. Payment Element supplies the details to stripe.confirmSetup with a return_url. A later on-session payment, while the customer is present and can authenticate, takes Customer and saved PaymentMethod IDs, EUR, payment_details[location] and the matching payment_details eligibility field in a separate server PaymentIntent. The example requests confirmation with confirm=true. An active location, a return URL and a confirmation request alone establish neither eligible classification nor successful authorization, capture or settlement (new raw lines 35-71).

November's sandbox keeps the Bimpli with Conecs test card, any three-digit CVC and any future expiration, but uses a PaymentLocation ID from onboarding in that same sandbox. Both captures describe possible issuer verification during saving, reflected as a temporary EUR 0.30 statement entry that Stripe reverses almost immediately and restores to the daily balance. This is conditional card verification, distinct from a completed voucher purchase or refund (old raw lines 75-92, new raw lines 73-85).

The mapped May 5 summary lines 13-36 captures saving, EUR on-session reuse and the temporary authorization, but it has only the historical direct-SIRET request shapes and fixtures. It also omits the issuer and onboarding scope and client confirmation handoff. Date its examples and add the November preview and server/client boundaries.
substantive_changes: The prerequisites and identity contract changed in the current guide. The restaurant's active PaymentLocation is selected separately for setup and charging, replacing the older direct nested SIRET inputs with the two location fields and the eligibility flag in each intent. November names the preview API version and private-preview request path (old raw lines 8-19,31-47,58-72 and new raw lines 9-29,35-44,53-70). The waitlist documents how to request access, not activation.

The test procedure changes from valid/invalid SIRET intent examples to the sandbox onboarding location and ID in the same sandbox. The Bimpli/Conecs card and the EUR 0.30 conditional verification behavior remain. Removing the old Elements variant banner, switching the SetupIntent snippet from Node to curl, and reformatting test headings and columns are presentation changes. The underlying UI remains Payment Element, and both November intent examples need preview version context despite omitting an explicit version header (old raw lines 21-54 and 75-92, new raw lines 25-51 and 61-85).

Retain supported issuers/private preview, client secret handoff with stripe.confirmSetup and return_url, later on-session EUR PaymentIntent with Customer and saved PaymentMethod, Bimpli sandbox test card and conditional EUR 0.30 temporary verification. Document the preview location contract alongside the old request shapes.

unresolved_questions: This pair does not establish legacy SIRET request-field availability for other versions or already provisioned accounts, required SDK library releases, response behavior for an ineligible payment method, a migration path for already saved methods, or off-session/recurring support. No preview enrollment, onboarding, API call or live payment was executed.

source_assessments.reason: The canonical guide materially changes onboarding, request identity and sandbox prerequisites. The mapped source presents the May request contract without version qualification and lacks the new preview and client/server details.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/meal-vouchers/fr-meal-vouchers/saving-payment-details, November documents saving French meal vouchers for Bimpli, Pluxee and Up Déjeuner in private preview. It requires Stripe API version 2026-05-27.preview or later and an API-onboarded PaymentLocation with active fr_meal_vouchers_conecs_payments. The server creates a SetupIntent with Customer ID, setup_details[location] and setup_details[benefit][fr_meal_voucher][enabled]=if_payment_method_is_eligible, then passes the client secret to Payment Element's stripe.confirmSetup flow with return_url. A later on-session EUR charge uses a separate PaymentIntent, Customer and saved PaymentMethod IDs, payment_details[location], the corresponding eligibility flag and confirm=true in the example. Sandbox setup takes a location ID from the same sandbox. An issuer verification may appear as a temporary 0.30 EUR authorization that is reversed almost immediately (new raw lines 9-51 and new raw lines 53-85). The May 5 capture and source-stripe-fr-meal-vouchers-save-payment.md use a pre-provisioned SIRET in each intent and older test SIRET examples. They share the SetupIntent versus on-session PaymentIntent split, EUR, test card and conditional authorization behavior (old raw lines 19-54 and old raw lines 56-92).
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/meal-vouchers/fr-meal-vouchers/saving-payment-details, the preview access and version terms, active per-location capability, location and eligibility parameters on both intents, and sandbox input are substantive (new raw lines 9-44 and new raw lines 53-81). The Node-to-curl switch and Elements variant banner removal are presentational. Date the May direct-SIRET setup and payment parameters and provisioned/invalid test SIRETs in source-stripe-fr-meal-vouchers-save-payment.md (old raw lines 19-54 and old raw lines 56-92). Cross-link the two contracts and distinguish the preview location's registered SIRET and possible onboarding review from the older Dashboard-managed record. Keep the companion accept-payment CVC and PaymentIntent SIRET-at-confirmation claims specific to that path. The documented preview version requirement applies even though the new curl examples omit a version header. The client receives the SetupIntent client secret, while server requests use the secret key. A waitlist request, location activation, client redirect and conditional verification do not establish a successful purchase, capture, settlement or off-session eligibility.
